changes.before: Implement toFinite(text) for string inputs. Reject blank text and non-finite conversions with null. Otherwise return Number(text); do not use parseInt to silently accept a numeric prefix.
changes.after: Turn the whole text into a number, rejecting blank text and invalid results.

before: Number(text) converts the whole string to a Number; surrounding whitespace is allowed. Empty or whitespace-only text converts to zero, so a form may deliberately reject that case first. String(value) returns a text representation without changing the original value.

parseInt(text, 10) reads an integer prefix in base ten. For "12px" it returns 12, while Number("12px") returns NaN, a special invalid-number value. Neither rule is universally the right validation policy. Number.isFinite(value) returns true only for a finite Number, not Infinity, NaN or a numeric string.

toFinite receives a string. trim() returns a new string with surrounding whitespace removed. Reject a blank cleaned string, then use Number and Number.isFinite. Return the finite numeric value or null; this policy uses Number syntax, including an explicit hexadecimal string such as "0x10".
Implement toFinite(text) for string inputs. Reject blank text and non-finite conversions with null. Otherwise return Number(text); do not use parseInt to silently accept a numeric prefix.
after:
`Number(text)` tries to convert the whole string into a number. It allows spaces at the edges.

Blank text becomes 0, so this exercise rejects it first. `String(value)` goes the other way: it makes a text version without changing the original value.

`parseInt(text, 10)` reads a whole-number beginning using base ten. For `"12px"`, it gives 12. `Number("12px")` instead gives `NaN`, meaning not a number.

`Number.isFinite` accepts actual numbers other than NaN and Infinity. It rejects numeric-looking strings too.

First trim and reject blank text. Then convert with `Number` and check `Number.isFinite`.

This follows Number's text rules, not just decimal digits. For example, `"0x10"` means 16 written in hexadecimal, a base-16 number system.

Complete `toFinite(text)`. Return the converted number when it is finite; otherwise return `null`.

Reject blank text. Do not use `parseInt` to accept only the beginning of invalid text.

after.question: Why is `parseInt("4.5tail", 10)` wrong when you must check the whole value?
choices: It accepts the beginning 4 instead of rejecting the text.
It always throws an error for extra text.
after.explanation: `parseInt` stops after the integer beginning. The rule here requires the whole text to become a finite Number.
